title: Control plane: config surface for perf-canary target models (by region/tier) + validation + audit logging
author: Connor O'Brien
release_notes: Adds a control-plane config object for perf-canary target model selection by region and capacity tier, with guardrails (validation + fanout limits) and audit logging for all changes.
body: Summary: This PR adds a first-class control-plane config surface for defining which models the perf-canary should exercise, scoped by region + capacity tier, with strict validation and audit logging. This unblocks phase-1 rollout in us-east with a small model set and gives SRE/runtime a safe way to expand coverage without code changes. Motivation: We need a single source of truth for the canary target list that (a) is auditable, (b) prevents accidental wide fanout (capacity burn / metric cardinality), and (c) allows staged rollout per region and tier. Previously, target lists were hardcoded in service config and required redeploys; that’s too risky for fast tuning. Design overview: Introduces a new config kind PerfCanaryTargets stored in the control-plane config service. Adds an admin write API (RBAC-gated) for setting/updating targets and a read API scoped to the perf-canary service account. The config is keyed by (region, tier) and contains a small list of model refs (canonical model_id + optional pinned model_version), plus optional per-target overrides (enabled flag, qps_budget, max_concurrency). All writes emit an audit event containing actor, request_id, before/after hashes, and a compact diff summary. Validation / guardrails: Validation happens on write in control plane. Rules: (1) tier must be one of: hosted-shared | dedicated | private; (2) region must be a known runtime region from the region registry; (3) max 10 targets per (region,tier); (4) qps_budget must be <= 0.2 QPS per target by default unless an explicit override is provided and the requestor has the perf_canary.admin_override capability; (5) each model_id must resolve via model-registry to a canonical model slug and is normalized to the canonical id; (6) if model_version is provided, it must exist and be runnable in that region (model-registry capability check); (7) duplicate model_id+version pairs are rejected; (8) config payload size is capped and validated to avoid accidental huge lists. Audit logging: All create/update/delete operations produce an AuditEvent {event_type=PERF_CANARY_TARGETS_CONFIG_CHANGED} and include: actor_user/actor_service, request_id, region, tier, old_config_hash, new_config_hash, change_summary, and a list of model ids affected (capped to 25; remainder summarized). Audit events go to the existing audit-log sink and are also emitted in structured logs for quick grep during incidents. Auth/RBAC: New permissions: perf_canary.targets.read (granted to perf-canary SA) and perf_canary.targets.write (granted to Runtime + SRE admin groups). The read endpoint is intentionally narrow (read-only, no list-all across regions unless caller has admin). API shape (internal): GET /internal/control-plane/v1/perf-canary/targets?region=us-east&tier=hosted-shared returns the resolved config (canonical ids) plus an etag. PUT /internal/control-plane/v1/perf-canary/targets?region=...&tier=... sets full config (replace semantics). Response includes validation warnings (non-fatal) and etag. Example payload (illustrative): {"targets": [{"model_id": "llama-3.1-8b-instruct", "model_version": "2026-01-10", "enabled": true, "qps_budget": 0.05}, {"model_id": "qwen2.5-7b-instruct", "enabled": true}], "defaults": {"max_concurrency": 2}}. Notes: The perf-canary service will consume this via its existing control-plane client (separate PR in perf-canary repo wires the new endpoint). This PR focuses only on control-plane surface area, validation, and auditability. Rollout plan: Feature-flagged behind control_plane.perf_canary_targets_config (default off). Once merged, we’ll enable in staging, seed us-east/hosted-shared with 2 targets, and verify canary reads + audit trails. Follow-ups: (1) add UI in Console for editing targets (tracked separately); (2) add optional per-SKU allowlists as we expand beyond phase-1; (3) add explicit “high-risk model” tagging once the model registry exposes it.
commits: control-plane: add PerfCanaryTargets config kind + store interface
control-plane: implement validation rules + canonical model id normalization
audit: emit PERF_CANARY_TARGETS_CONFIG_CHANGED on writes with diff summary
docs/tests: add validation and audit unit tests + internal runbook
conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we avoid exposing model_version as free-form? Worried about pinning leading to stale baselines / unexpected drift. Also, please confirm we’re not adding new high-cardinality labels anywhere in control plane logs. Connor O'Brien (author): Agreed on the risk; model_version is optional and validation checks it’s runnable in-region. The canary defaults to unpinned (latest stable) unless explicitly set. No new metrics labels in this PR; audit logs include model ids in a capped list and otherwise a count summary. Nadia Rahman (review): For the read endpoint: can we include an etag so the canary can cache + avoid hot-polling? Connor O'Brien: Yep—added etag derived from config hash. Response includes etag and server sets Cache-Control: private,max-age=30 for read calls. Allison Grant (review): Audit event needs request_id and actor fields standardized. Please use the shared AuditContext helper so incident-bot / SRE tooling can correlate changes. Connor O'Brien: Updated to use AuditContext; request_id is pulled from gateway middleware and actor is resolved from auth context (user vs service). Noah Patel (review): Validation max 10 targets per (region,tier) seems fine, but we should cap concurrency defaults too; otherwise someone could set qps_budget low but crank concurrency high and still add overhead. Connor O'Brien: Added defaults.max_concurrency validation (<= 4) and per-target override cap (<= 8) gated behind perf_canary.admin_override. Quentin Harris (review): Model id normalization should use canonical model registry id, not the display slug. Also ensure we’re checking capability by region/tier (some models not enabled in Dedicated). Connor O'Brien: Fixed—now we store canonical model_id from registry and validate region+tier availability via registry capability endpoint. CI: First run failed due to a missing generated swagger artifact; reran after adding generation step to presubmit, now green. Approvals: Noah Patel approved; Logan Wright approved; Nadia Rahman approved; Allison Grant approved with nit addressed. Merged via squash on 2026-01-22.
